findings.claim: The rival's rejection rests on an undigited genericity claim whose swept object is blended: the form actually shared across the seam is word-bound in exactly 2 verses book-wide, both of them this seam's own verses.
findings.grounds: הָ֝אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Prov.27.19) and הָ֝אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Prov.27.20) each collate byte at their own cited ref and are byte-identical to one another, and that definite form is word-bound in exactly 2 verses in the whole book (consonantal_index.json word-bound scan: Prov.27.19 and Prov.27.20, i.e. this seam's own two verses). The bare lexeme is a different object: 33 word-bound verses, and sweep.py --skel returns 44 verses / 46 token occurrences for the contiguous substring. observed_substrate_signals blends the two, calling it the shared skeleton token of the bare lexeme 'as' the definite form, and no digit appears anywhere in the row. Measured against the row's own comparanda the comparison inverts: זָ֭הָב is word-bound in 4 verses (11:22, 20:15, 25:11, 25:12), עָ֭צֵל in 12 verses plus וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל at 26:14, and הָג֣וֹ in 2 verses (25:4, 25:5) - so the form actually shared here is as narrow as the narrowest catchword the row calls narrower, and narrower than two of the three.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: re-state the rejection with the object named and the digits given (definite form 2 word-bound verses book-wide, both at this seam; bare lexeme 33 word-bound verses / 44 substring verses), and re-derive the comparison, which inverts against two of the three cited catchwords. Routed onward, not adjudicated here: with the corrected digit the proverb_cluster rival at Prov.27.19-Prov.27.20 rests on a byte-grounded catchword of exactly the kind the cluster bar admits and must be re-weighed against the two similes' semantic independence; no span change is proposed by this auditor.

triggers.grounds: Well calibrated, and the low band is if anything conservative. The seam warrants are tier-1 and byte-verified: oshb:Prov.30.1 opens with the construct header דִּבְרֵ֤י paired with הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א (both collate byte at Prov.30.1), which is the ruled collection-seam spine for C6. Every digit in the row re-derives exactly: sweep.py --skel returns 19 verses for the unpointed skeleton and that set is identical to the row's own 9 construct + 6 suffixed + 4 absolute-plural enumeration; the construct opens the verse in exactly 5 of the 19 (Prov.12.6, Prov.18.8, Prov.26.22, Prov.30.1, Prov.31.1, first-token check on consonantal_index.json); and exactly 2 of those 5 pair with an oracle word (Prov.30.1 and Prov.31.1). oshb:Prov.29.27 and oshb:Prov.30.1 share zero word-bound skeleton tokens. pmarks_Prov.json records PE at Prov.29.27 and Prov.30.6 - petuchah, single witness, correctly typed, never conflated with the one SAMEKH at Prov.24.22, and disclosed as single-witness in both refs (check_marks GREEN, citation_sweep GREEN). The band tracks the real crux the row discloses and refuses to resolve, the doubled name-form לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל at oshb:Prov.30.1, and frontier_flag_considered is true; the book's own expected-low-confidence register names 30:1 for exactly this reason. Nothing in the row's evidence is over-claimed and no defect found below touches a seam, so the band is honest rather than a label masking a defective warrant.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals and device_notes label 30:2-5 a first-person confession, which is byte-false at 30:4-5 and contradicts the row's own rationale.
findings.grounds: First-person forms stand only in oshb:Prov.30.2 (אָנֹכִ֣י, לִֽי) and oshb:Prov.30.3 (לָמַ֥דְתִּי, אֵדָֽע). oshb:Prov.30.4 closes second-person, כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע, and oshb:Prov.30.5 is third person throughout, מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ - which the row's own boundary_rationale gets right by separating the 30:2-4 meditation from the 30:5 affirmation. observed_substrate_signals ('the confession spanning 30:2-5') and device_notes ('first-person confessional (30:2-5)') therefore contradict both the driver field and the bytes. The operative claim inside that signal - that the passage opens without a numeral or vocative formula - is true either way.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: label the first-person confession 30:2-3 in observed_substrate_signals and device_notes, keeping the rationale's own 30:2-4 meditation / 30:5 affirmation division. No span change: the unit's bounds are unaffected.

findings.claim: The header gloss renders the name that the splice elides, so gloss extent exceeds splice extent.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale splices דִּבְרֵ֤י ... הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א (each collates byte at oshb:Prov.30.1) and glosses the pair 'the words of Agur ... the oracle'. The name אָג֥וּר falls inside the elision, so the gloss renders a token the splice does not carry and gloss extent exceeds splice extent.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: either splice דִּבְרֵ֤י אָג֥וּר ... הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א or cut the gloss to 'the words of ... the oracle'.

findings.claim: The 19-verse digit is attached to a pointed byte-tier run whose own byte form occurs in one verse.
findings.grounds: The row writes that 'the skeleton' דִּבְרֵ֤י occurs in 19 verses book-wide. The displayed run is byte tier (collate byte at oshb:Prov.30.1) and its NFC-normalised byte form occurs in exactly 1 verse of verse_map_oshb.json, Prov.30.1; the 19 belongs to the unpointed contiguous-substring skeleton, which sweep.py --skel confirms at 19 verses, set-identical to the row's enumeration. Object and label are mismatched; the digit itself is right, and no tier is over-claimed (skeleton is the weaker label, not the stronger).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: write the swept form unpointed, or phrase it as the skeleton of דִּבְרֵ֤י, so the displayed object matches the digit.

findings.claim: The vetitive construction runs continuously across the row's closing seam and is not disclosed.
findings.grounds: The row quotes its closing warning אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָ֑יו at oshb:Prov.30.6 but does not note that the same vetitive particle heads the next two verses: אַל תִּמְנַ֥ע at oshb:Prov.30.7 and אַל תִּֽתֶּן at oshb:Prov.30.8 (the identical patach form at all three, distinct from the preposition that also stands at oshb:Prov.30.10). A byte-true construction straddling the row's own closing seam is an unconditional disclosure obligation. The seam still holds on the numeral opener שְׁ֭תַּיִם at oshb:Prov.30.7, which the row correctly names as the next unit's beginning.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose the straddling vetitive chain at oshb:Prov.30.6, oshb:Prov.30.7 and oshb:Prov.30.8 and state why the numeral opener at 30:7 outweighs it. No span change proposed.

triggers.grounds: Well calibrated, and the stated reason is byte-checkable and honest. device_notes holds the band at medium_low because the seam rests on a register shift, with the petuchah only corroborating and the petition sitting inside the same first-person Agur material - and the bytes agree, since oshb:Prov.30.7 is itself first-person speech (שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי, מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי, אָמֽוּת), exactly like oshb:Prov.30.2 and oshb:Prov.30.3. The mark claims are sound: pmarks_Prov.json records PE at Prov.30.6 and Prov.30.9, petuchah, single witness, correctly typed and disclosed at both, never conflated with the one SAMEKH at Prov.24.22 (check_marks GREEN, citation_sweep GREEN). The exclusivity digit is true at the object it names: the divine name is word-bound in 70 verses and 70 token occurrences book-wide and stands once in ch 30, at oshb:Prov.30.9 (מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה, collate byte), while the contiguous-substring sweep returns 87 verses - so the row's 70 is the exact-token object the book's density figures use, not a mis-swept digit. The numeral opener שְׁ֭תַּיִם at oshb:Prov.30.7 is a genuine tier-1 signal the row could have leaned on harder, so the band understates rather than masks. The defects recorded below sit in the warrant's phrasing and in undisclosed straddling devices; neither makes medium_low the wrong band.

findings.claim: The register map that carries the rival's rejection is byte-false at 30:4-5 and blends speaker-person with addressee-person.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative rejects merging 30:7-9 into the preceding unit on '30:1-6's 3rd-person narration (30:1) and 1st-person confession before God (30:2-5)'. First-person forms stand only at oshb:Prov.30.2 (אָנֹכִ֣י, לִֽי) and oshb:Prov.30.3 (לָמַ֥דְתִּי, אֵדָֽע); oshb:Prov.30.4 closes second-person, כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע, and oshb:Prov.30.5 is third person throughout, מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ. The contrast also blends two categories: 30:7 is itself first-person speech (שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי, מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי, אָמֽוּת), so what changes at the seam is the addressee - human at oshb:Prov.30.6 (בְּךָ֣) to God at oshb:Prov.30.7 (מֵאִתָּ֑ךְ) - not the speaker's person. Since the row names the register shift as 'the seam's real warrant', the rejection's stated ground is byte-false as written, though it is repairable and the seam itself survives on the numeral opener שְׁ֭תַּיִם.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: state the register facts as the bytes have them - first-person confession at 30:2-3, third-person affirmation at 30:5, and an addressee shift from a human audience to God at the 30:6|30:7 seam inside continuous first-person speech - and let the numeral opener at oshb:Prov.30.7 carry the rejection. No span change: the seam stands.

findings.claim: Byte-true construction chains straddle both of the row's seams undisclosed, and the following verse is called unrelated against them.
findings.grounds: Opening edge: the vetitive particle heads oshb:Prov.30.6 (אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ), oshb:Prov.30.7 (אַל תִּמְנַ֥ע) and oshb:Prov.30.8 (אַל תִּֽתֶּן), the particle byte-identical at all three (collate byte at each ref). Closing edge: the lest-particle recurs at the skeleton tier - the forms differ in accent and one in prefix, so this is a skeleton-tier claim and not byte identity - at oshb:Prov.30.6 (פֶּן), twice at oshb:Prov.30.9 (פֶּ֥ן and וּפֶֽן) and again at oshb:Prov.30.10 (פֶּֽן), where the same vetitive also opens the verse (אַל תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן; the preposition אֶל in the same verse is the homograph and is not counted). Neither chain appears in boundary_rationale, observed_substrate_signals or device_notes, while the row asserts a clean register break at the opening edge and calls the following verse an 'unrelated servant/slander saying' - an overstatement against a shared vetitive opener and a shared lest-particle. The standing cross-seam rule makes a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam a disclosure obligation at both edges.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose both chains with their refs and argue the seams against them, since both survive (the numeral opener at oshb:Prov.30.7 and the petuchah-corroborated close at oshb:Prov.30.9); drop or qualify 'unrelated' for Prov.30.10. No span change proposed by this auditor, but the strengthened merge rival at Prov.30.1-Prov.30.9 is routed onward with the corrected disclosure.

findings.claim: The driver field says the petuchah 'marks that seam', which is driver-shaped language for a tier-3 single-witness mark and contradicts the row's own other two statements about it.
findings.grounds: pmarks_Prov.json records PE at Prov.30.6, single witness, and the Writings parashah layer is tier-3 weak corroboration that is never a boundary driver. boundary_rationale nonetheless says the petuchah at 30:6 'marks that seam', while strongest_rejected_alternative calls it 'a non-driver petuchah at 30:6' and device_notes says it 'corroborates without independently marking a break at exactly this seam'. The mark is real, correctly typed and single-witness disclosed, so the defect is driver-shaped phrasing in the driver field, contradicted by the row's own two other statements about the same mark.
